review_summary: The junior differential captured the major disease clusters and explained all high‑severity lab abnormalities. Probability weighting needed adjustment (increase metabolic‑syndrome, decrease FH and CKD). Important missing data (spirometry, iron studies, thyroid panel, sleep assessment) limit certainty for several secondary diagnoses. Overall reasoning quality is good but could be strengthened by tighter probability calibration and inclusion of a few plausible differentials (e.g., secondary hypothyroid dyslipidaemia, early myelodysplastic process).
